subtopics.title: Botha's Reforms, the Tricameral Parliament and the United Democratic Front

questions.question: Who became Prime Minister of South Africa in 1978?
The Tricameral Parliament had separate houses for:
options: White, coloured and Indian people only

questions.question: The United Democratic Front was launched in 1983 at:
Why did many coloured and Indian people reject the Tricameral Parliament?
options: Because it gave them too much power
Because they saw it as a way to divide them from Africans and legitimise apartheid
Because they wanted to be part of the homelands

subtopics.title: Internal Resistance and the Township Uprisings

questions.question: The township uprising of 1984 began in the:
What did the 1984 Vaal protests target first?
options: Rent increases by Black Local Authorities

questions.question: Inkatha was led by:
Why did many UDF and church leaders condemn necklacing?
options: Because it was approved by the government
Because it was a cruel killing, often without fair trial, that divided communities

subtopics.title: Repression: States of Emergency, Detentions and Covert Killings

questions.question: A national state of emergency was declared on:
Who were the Cradock Four?
options: Activists abducted and murdered by security police in 1985
Four soldiers who refused to fight

questions.question: The Civil Cooperation Bureau was:
options: A secret military unit that killed and kidnapped activists

questions.question: Why did repression fail to end resistance in the 1980s?
options: Because new resistance kept emerging, such as the Mass Democratic Movement by 1989
Because the government released everyone in 1986
Because the army refused to enter townships

subtopics.title: External Pressure and the Road to Negotiations, and the Error Museum

questions.question: Botha's speech of 15 August 1985 is known as the:
Which country's Congress passed the Comprehensive Anti-Apartheid Act in 1986?
Which statement is correct?
options: The Tricameral Parliament gave Africans the vote
Mandela held secret talks with the government while in prison
All violence in the 1980s came from one side

questions.question: Why did the end of the Cold War make negotiations easier?
options: It made the ANC stronger militarily
It weakened the government's claim of a communist threat and reduced Soviet support for armed struggle

questions.question: In the Simplifier story, the "parliament with three doors" had no door for:
Hundreds of groups united to form the:
The giant union federation formed in 1985 was:
The Vaal uprising began on:
A consumer boycott meant:
options: Refusing to buy from white-owned shops to apply pressure

questions.question: Under the states of emergency, the police could:
options: Only arrest people with a warrant
Detain people without trial and restrict the media

questions.question: Why did the government use the army inside townships?
options: Because the police alone could not control the scale of the uprisings
Because the army was trained to teach in schools
Because the townships asked for soldiers
Because there was a war with Angola inside Soweto

questions.question: Which bank refused to roll over South Africa's loans in 1985?
Who replaced P.W. Botha as State President in 1989?
Namibia became independent in:
What is the main idea of this lesson?
options: Internal resistance, repression and external pressure created a crisis that pushed both sides toward negotiation
The UDF supported the Tricameral Parliament
